clue.text: Private papers in good order

indicators.note: putting the letters into good order means rearranging them into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Confidential documents are filed neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective about the papers, but it is a soldier's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a private soldier in the Royal Engineers, the lowest rank there.

clue.text: Grave expression of appreciation

parts.note: a tribute to the dead, carved where they are buried, with 'grave' read as the burial place rather than solemn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' seems to mean serious; it is the tomb on which the words are inscribed.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tombstone praises the person buried beneath it.

clue.text: A woman caught over attitude adopted

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
on means over, as in resting on top of
a stance is a posture or attitude taken up

explanation.surface: A woman is caught striking a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female first name.

clue.text: Mature about the City's way of doing things

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: ripe means fully mature
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Ripening around the financial district describes its habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a method or formula for achieving something, not only cooking.

clue.text: Stake a pound by mail

parts.note: a post is a stake driven into the ground
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone wagers a pound by sending it through the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' looks like a bet; it is a wooden post.
explanation.definitionFit: Postal describes something sent through the post, by mail.

clue.text: It's normal to cut the talk

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level, as in golf
to lance is to cut open with a blade

explanation.surface: Cutting a conversation short is considered standard practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a manner of speaking, the way people talk.

clue.text: Bearing with an island race, none will cause contention

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
O, zero, means none

explanation.surface: A compass heading, an island and a race with no winner provoke a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a fight or argument, a bout of contention.

clue.text: The agreeable person a fool put down

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to enter is to put down in writing, to record

explanation.surface: A pleasant person dismissed someone as an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: One who agrees or consents to something is an agreeable person in that sense.

clue.text: Bad lads hope to make such a bloomer!

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoilt and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Naughty boys hope to make a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a plant that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family plant that flowers, so a bloomer.

clue.text: Object: getting a tiresome fellow to admit corruption

indicators.note: admitting means letting the second piece inside the first

parts.note: a pest is a tiresome, annoying person
rot means decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Someone objects when a nuisance is made to confess wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to complain or raise a formal complaint against it.

clue.text: Heads bringing the heartless into step

indicators.note: into means the shortened word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: pas is a step in ballet

indicators.note: heartless means the word loses its middle, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Leaders bring the cruel into line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle H from THE, leaving TE, which goes into PAS, the dance step.
explanation.definitionFit: Pates is an old word for heads, especially the tops of them.

clue.text: Back strike-a rise is most important!

indicators.note: back means the word for strike is read from right to left

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
to mount is to rise or climb

explanation.surface: Supporting a strike and a pay rise is the top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like support, but it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, ranking above all others.

clue.text: Skill in driving car-the thing is to be alert

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the word that follows, across the hyphen

explanation.surface: Driving well means staying alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean skill or craft, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: He'll quote devastating repartee

indicators.note: devastating suggests the word is wrecked and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: A man will cite some crushing banter.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is one who says something again, repeating what was said.

clue.text: Cried out as entitled

definitions.meaning: shouted, as in calling for help
named, as in a book bearing a title

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: shouted aloud, and given a name or title.

clue.text: Love getting an allowance after some trouble

indicators.note: after puts the allowance behind the trouble in the answer

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Romance follows a struggle over money.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship.

clue.text: Stiff and sore maybe, and kind of yellow

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone with aching limbs looks jaundiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Primrose is a pale yellow colour, named after the flower.

clue.text: Loaf and get the bird

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a round bread loaf, and the male of the swan.

clue.text: General's heraldic device

definitions.meaning: a simple geometric charge on a coat of arms

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: commonplace, and a basic charge such as a bend or chevron in heraldry.

clue.text: About five hundred are in colour

parts.note: re means about or concerning
D is the Roman numeral for 500; the colour also sits inside the word hundred, but that is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Around five hundred items are dyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is one shade of this primary colour.

clue.text: Support Her Majesty, as is only right

parts.note: a prop supports something
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Backing the monarch is the correct thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means fitting or correct, as is right.

clue.text: Small house offering sleeping accommodation

definitions.meaning: a baby's bed or a camp bed

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a little dwelling, and a small bed.

clue.text: To close up when in a crowd would be sheer lunacy!

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the crowd

parts.note: a mass is a crowd

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: Shutting oneself in among a crowd would be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading the word for close from the bottom upwards; 'To' and 'when' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is insanity or extreme folly.

clue.text: In public accountants appear far from sunny

indicators.note: in means the accountants go inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
CA is a chartered accountant, so CAs are accountants

explanation.surface: Accountants seen in public look gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast describes a cloudy sky, the opposite of sunny weather.

clue.text: The dealer drove all over the place around the North

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the N
scattered all over the place means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A trader drove everywhere around northern parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is a seller, one who deals in goods.

clue.text: Set about obtaining weight-lifting equipment

definitions.meaning: to start dealing with a task
ropes and pulleys for hoisting loads

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to take on a job, and a pulley system for raising weights.

clue.text: Present one made time to exchange

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: exchanging the letters swaps them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone created a slot to swap a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it means happening now.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means happening at once, in the current moment.

clue.text: Stand up before the court, in short

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Rise before the judges enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright, standing tall.

clue.text: Drink-put some of it on ice

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pour a little of the mixer over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Drink-put' as the definition; 'put' is the link to the hidden run, so the definition is just 'Drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a mixer drink, often with gin.

clue.text: Tom from Eastern Europe?

parts.note: a male cat from Poland, read whimsically as the name of a weasel-like animal

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as Pole plus cat: a tom is a male cat, and a Pole comes from Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Great disadvantage in solid fuel

indicators.note: in means the disadvantage goes inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
a loss is a disadvantage or setback

explanation.surface: A major setback hits the coal industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means huge, enormously large.

clue.text: Aristocrats demanding information before trial

indicators.note: before puts the information ahead of the trial

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a try is an attempt or trial

explanation.surface: Nobles demand details ahead of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the upper class, people of good birth.
